record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training and validation error while varying BatchNorm statistics and normalization batch size. These tests bear on generalization gaps, but normalization batch size is distinct from the SGD batch size in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own BatchNorm experiments. Results cited from prior work, including the cited ImageNet training recipe, are not recorded as findings. Versioned claims do not cover the normalization-batch-size sweep, so those findings are listed under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own ImageNet ResNet-50 validation errors for SGD batches of 256 and 8192 at the same 100-epoch budget, following Goyal et al.'s recipe. This directly tests V5, alongside its separate BatchNorm investigations.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that careful construction of BatchNorm batches and consistency between training and inference can prevent degraded performance. Their review covers inaccurate EMA statistics, normalization batch size, domain mismatch, and information leakage between correlated samples, with remedies demonstrated in classification and detection.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies BatchNorm statistics and normalization batch size, rather than reproducing the original random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, or regularization experiments. Its matched large-SGD-batch comparison uses ImageNet ResNet-50 and EMA or PreciseBN evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation behavior depends on the BatchNorm normalization batch size and on whether evaluation uses EMA, PreciseBN, or mini-batch statistics. PreciseBN results also vary with the number of samples and the batch size used to forward them.

fits_no_version.finding: With SGD batch size fixed at 1024, the authors report that the training-to-validation gap under mini-batch-statistics evaluation decreases as normalization batch size increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BatchNorm normalization batch size affects generalization gaps independently of SGD batch size.

record.problems: Figure 5 reports the normalization-batch-size generalization-gap trend without numerical values in the supplied text. The matched SGD-batch-size comparison reports a small error difference and no uncertainty for the EMA values. The 30-epoch large-batch condition in Table 1 has no 256-batch, 30-epoch counterpart, so it is not used as a matched comparison.

relationships.reason: Only a small residual penalty remains: 24.0% versus 23.7% with EMA (R1–R2), and 23.73% versus 23.54% with PreciseBN (R3), qualifying the magnitude of the penalty under this recipe.
relationships.display_finding: Error increased from 23.7% to 24.0% with exponential moving averages (EMA) and from 23.54% to 23.73% with precise batch normalization (PreciseBN). PreciseBN variability came from selecting evaluation samples rather than from independent training runs.
